text.p: Shares in French pharmaceuticals and beauty products group Sanofi rallied in a higher market on Thursday on bullish comments made at a general meeting on Wednesday, dealers said.
At 0911 GMT, Sanofi traded 6.40 percent higher at 549 francs while the blue-chip index was up 1.99 percent.
Sanofi chairman Jean-Francois Dehecq said on Wednesday that the rise in the 1997 results could be in line with the increase in 1996.
"A favourable start to 1997 allows us to believe that, if nothing changes," the increase in 1997 results "will be of the same order of magnitude" as for 1996, he told the annual shareholders meeting.
Sanofi, in which Elf Aquitaine holds a 55 percent stake, reported an 11 percent increase in 1996 net profit to 1.74 billion francs and saw turnover rising 3.2 percent to 23.64 billion francs.
He said Sanofi was optimistic about its main drugs and said results of beauty products were improving in a difficult market. -- Paris newsroom +33 1 4221 5452
